info.title: IMEI-HUB API: internal reference
info.description:
Every route of the API: admin console, merchant portal, storefront, Dhru Fusion, incoming webhooks and system routes. Generated from the route contracts; the public subset is `/openapi.json`.

Each operation shows its access kind (`x-gsm-access`), the permission a staff route needs (`x-gsm-permission`) and the manifest key (`x-gsm-key`).

**Conventions.** JSON bodies use camelCase names. Money is a string with exactly four decimals (`"12.4900"`), timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`"2026-03-01T09:30:00.000Z"`) and ids are numbers. Errors are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`; quote the `requestId` when you contact support.

**Supplier calls.** Calls this backend makes to a supplier's Dhru Fusion API (`POST <supplier>/api/index.php`); they are no routes of this API. Schemas and examples are in `x-gsm-supplier-calls`.

- `accountinfo`: Our balance at the supplier.
- `imeiservicelist`: The supplier's services and their cost.
- `placeimeiorder`: Send an order to the supplier. Bulk variant `placeimeiorderbulk`: never sent.
- `getimeiorder`: Ask the supplier for the status of an order. Bulk variant `getimeiorderbulk`: never sent.

put.description: Stores the setting `adminAllowlistOnly`. Turning it on is `409 IP_NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST` unless a live allow rule covers the caller's own address, so nobody locks themselves out. Turning it off is always allowed. Idempotent. A caller who is not an owner gets `403 FORBIDDEN` when turning it on would shut out an address an active owner uses (decision 046). The change is judged as things are and at each later moment a rule runs out: an owner's address may not be refused at any moment at which it would have been allowed without the change.

post.description: Every field is required except `isActive` (default true). `key` is unique among the rules that are not deleted (a duplicate is `422` on `key`). `metric` is one of the ten registry keys and the server sets `unit` from it: `supplier.timeout_rate`, `supplier.error_rate`, `api.rate5xx`, `db.connection_usage` and `redis.memory_usage` are `percent`; `api.p95` is `ms`; `queue.oldest_age` is `s`; `orders.past_sla` and `ledger.mismatch_count` are `count`; `supplier.balance` has no unit (`null`). `threshold` is a number in that unit. `windowSeconds` (60 to 86400) is the period a rate or percentile is measured over (`supplier.timeout_rate`, `supplier.error_rate`, `api.p95`, `api.rate5xx`); for `supplier.balance`, `queue.oldest_age`, `orders.past_sla`, `db.connection_usage` and `redis.memory_usage`, which read the moment, it is how long the condition must hold: the alert opens after every evaluation of the whole window was over the threshold and closes after every evaluation of the whole window was back in range. `ledger.mismatch_count` is the result of the newest integrity run and ignores the window. `channels` is a non-empty list of `telegram` and `email`. Writes the audit entry `added alert rule`.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change, and each is checked like on create. `isActive: false` resolves the rule's open alerts. `mutedUntil` (a future time) mutes the rule: it opens no new alerts until then, alerts already open stay open and still close by themselves; `null` unmutes; a past or invalid time is `422` on `mutedUntil`. A new `metric` recomputes `unit` and resolves the open alerts of the old metric. Writes the audit entry `changed alert rule` (`muted alert rule`, `unmuted alert rule`, `turned on alert rule` or `turned off alert rule` when that is all that changed).

get.description: Newest first. Filters: `status` (`firing`, `acknowledged` or `resolved`; repeat the key for several), `severity`, and `open=true` (firing or acknowledged; `open=false` is resolved). `q` searches the rule name, the subject label and the note. `rule` is the snapshot taken when the alert fired, so a later edit or delete of the rule never rewrites it; `rule.id` and `rule.key` are live. An acknowledged alert stays open (and counts in the health page, critical included) until the value is back in range. During a database outage the route answers `503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`.

patch.description: A partial body with at least one key: `rateLimitPerMin` (an integer from 1 to 6000) and `allowedIps` (up to 20 addresses or ranges; `[]` removes the restriction). Takes effect on the next call with the key: its cached view is dropped after the commit. A change that gives the key more reach (an empty list, an address that is not stored, a higher limit) needs an owner: `403 FORBIDDEN` for everyone else, judged on the stored key; a narrower list or a lower limit stays under `api_keys:update`. A revoked key is `409 ALREADY_REVOKED`. Writes the audit entry `changed limits of API key of <merchant>` with the old and new values; a change of a value sends the merchant a security notice by email.

post.description: The last sign-in step: it turns the pending session into a full one (a new session token). The sign-in is recorded in the audit log by this step. Twenty wrong codes of one account within 24 hours close the step: every code, the right one included, is then refused with `429 RATE_LIMITED`, whose `Retry-After` is the seconds until it opens. post.description: The first sign-in step. It creates a pending session (10 minutes) and answers which step follows. A failed attempt is logged and rate-limited but writes no audit row; the sign-in is audited when the second step completes. Five attempts per email and network (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) in 15 minutes; ten failed attempts for one email (a success in between does not cancel them) lock it for 15 minutes for every network its account has not signed in from: both answer `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, the same for every email. While the lock runs, the attempts a network the account has signed in from is still allowed share one budget per network: five in 15 minutes, then `429 RATE_LIMITED` like any other attempt. A temporary password works for 72 hours after it was set; after that it is refused like a wrong password.

patch.description: Only the keys sent change (the console sends a diff). A new discount prices the next order of the merchants in the group; open orders keep their `pricing_snapshot`. `isDefault: true` moves the default mark here; `isDefault: false` on the default group is `409 DEFAULT_GROUP_REQUIRED` (make another group the default instead), and the storefront group cannot be the default (`422` on `isDefault`). `overdraftAllowed: false` is `422` on `overdraftAllowed` while any merchant of the group has a credit limit above zero (user rule 2); `overdraftAllowed: true` on the storefront retail rank is `422` on `overdraftAllowed` (code `retail_no_credit`: the retail rank never allows credit). A duplicate name is `422` on `name`.

delete.description: Refused with `409 GROUP_IN_USE` for the default group, the storefront retail group and a group that still has accounts (the detail says how many); the rank history of accounts never blocks it, because it keeps the names and kinds of both ranks without a foreign key. Otherwise, in one transaction: the group prices and the pricing rules of the group are deleted, its id is removed from the allowed groups of every service category, and the group is deleted. Orders keep their pricing snapshot, so no history is lost. One audit entry lists the removed pricing rule ids.

post.description: A fixed price one merchant pays for one service, from its next order: it beats the group price, the pricing rules and every discount. The price must be above zero and at or above the floor of the merchant's group (effective cost plus minimum profit): `422` on `price` with "Below the floor of $X (cost $Y plus $Z minimum profit).". patch.description: One kind of change per call: a status or details (a mix is `422` on the first key of the second kind). `status` is `active` (reactivate a suspended account) or `suspended` (with a `reason` of 3 to 140 characters); any other change is `409 INVALID_TRANSITION`, and `blocked` and `anonymized` have their own routes (`422` on `status`). Details are `name`, `company`, `phone`, `country`, `email`, `address`, `taxId` and `internalNotes` (several at once; a value equal to the stored one is not a change). A `groupId` is refused with `422` (field `groupId`, code `use_rank_route`): the rank changes through `POST /admin/clients/:id/rank`. Suspending, reactivating and changing the email of an account with a login also need `clients:security`; reactivating a merchant-rank account that was suspended because it was never approved needs the Owner (`403 FORBIDDEN`). A guest cannot take an email that another guest or an account with a login uses (`409 EMAIL_TAKEN`, code `taken`). Any write on an anonymized account is `409 ANONYMIZED`.

post.summary: Make an account of a guest

post.description: Irreversible, and for the retail rank only (`409 CONFLICT` "Move the account to the retail rank first." for a merchant rank). The account becomes `anonymized`: the name is "Deleted account", the email `deleted-account-<id>@redacted.invalid` (the old address is free again), the phone and internal notes are cleared, marketing is off and the account is closed (the password and the two-step secret are cleared, every session ended, every API key stopped, outstanding links voided). The IMEI on its orders and checkout sessions is cut to the TAC and a mask. Payments, ledger entries and amounts stay for accounting. The account’s open or in-progress erasure request is completed. When the account’s email is proven, the guest row of that email is erased in the same transaction with the same steps (an open checkout or a pending payment of that row refuses the whole erasure with `409 CONFLICT`). Audited as `anonymised account`, naming the account by number. Refused with `409 CONFLICT` while the store balance is not zero, a top-up waits for review or a top-up dispute is open; unpaid top-ups are voided.

post.description: Only for an `active` account of a merchant rank (`409 CONFLICT` for a retail rank, `409 NOT_ACTIVE` for a suspended, blocked or erased account: such a key could not be used). The body is the merchant's own creation plus `rateLimitPerMin` (an integer from 1 to 6000, default 60). The answer carries the full key once as `secret` (`Cache-Control: no-store`); only a keyed hash is stored, so a lost key cannot be shown again. The key is marked `createdByStaff` and `api_keys.created_by` records the staff member, the merchant is sent a security notice by email, and the audit entry `created API key for <merchant>` never holds the key. A merchant may hold 10 live keys: the next one is `422` on `name`. Only an owner may create one (`403 FORBIDDEN` for everyone else, decision 046); a merchant creates its own keys in the portal.

post.description: `{ blocked: true, reason }` blocks an account of any rank for fraud (use a suspension for a temporary stop); `{ blocked: false }` lifts the block (a reason is optional). Blocking sets the status `blocked`, ends every session, stops every API key, appends the reason to the internal notes, and adds to the blocklist, with source manual, the reason, the caller and the account: the email, each distinct card fingerprint of its payments and each distinct IMEI still stored on its shop orders and checkouts (never the IMEIs of portal or Dhru orders: a merchant orders for other people’s devices; an entry that already exists is kept as it is and not linked to this account). Unblocking sets `active` and deletes only the manual entries this account’s block added. `reason` must be one of: Chargeback or dispute; Card testing or fraud; Abuse of refunds; Other (422 on `reason` otherwise). Audited as `blocked account` or `unblocked account`.

parameters.description: Numeric record id.

reason.description: When blocking, one of: Chargeback or dispute; Card testing or fraud; Abuse of refunds; Other. When lifting, an optional note.

patch.description: Sets the overdraft limit of the merchant wallet; `0.0000` removes the credit. A limit above zero needs a rank that allows credit (`422` on `creditLimit` otherwise), and a store balance has no credit limit (`422` on `creditLimit`, `not_allowed`). Lowering the limit below the credit in use is allowed: new orders are refused until a top-up. Raising it on a wallet that is on hold is refused (`409 WALLET_FROZEN`). Raising the limit above the approval limit of adjustments (`wallet.adjust_approval_limit`, default $10,000) needs an Owner (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 049), and so does a raise that takes the staff member's credits to merchant wallets and credit-limit raises within 24 hours above it (the raised part counts); lowering it never does. A rank change of the same account and this change are judged one after the other. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required: a retry with the same key and body answers the first result (`idempotency-replayed: true`) and changes nothing twice; the same key with another body is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. No ledger entry; audited.

get.description: A JSON file (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="account-<id>.json"`, never cached) with everything the shop holds about the account, of any rank: the profile with its rank (and the company, address, tax id and username when it has them), the orders with their IMEI, the payments without card data, the consents, the checkout sessions, the support tickets with their public messages (only tickets whose requester's address is confirmed: a ticket opened on the contact form with a typed address is left out until its link is used), the data requests, the uploaded files (name and size) and, for a retail account, the store balance with its statement (`wallet`, staff reasons hidden). A merchant rank adds `merchant`: its wallet and statement, its API keys (label and dates, never a key or a hash) and its invoices. For a retail account whose email is proven, `ordersPlacedAsGuest` lists the orders, payments, checkouts, consents, tickets and files of the guest row of that email. It works for an anonymized account too. The export closes the account’s open or in-progress export request (`completed`, handled by the caller) and is audited as `exported data of`; no copy of the file is kept. Because a GET has this side effect and carries no CSRF token, the request must be started by the console itself (`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the console’s origins): anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED`.

post.description: `reset_link` emails the account a one-hour, one-use link (purpose `invite` while the account has no password, else `reset`; it replaces an older invitation or reset link) and answers which mail was sent in `link`; the current password keeps working until the link is used. The answer never carries the link. `temporary_password` generates and stores a password (hash only), forces a change at the next sign-in (the account meets `next: password` on sign-in), cancels older links, ends every session of the account, emails the account a security notice and returns the password once in `temporaryPassword`. Always `Cache-Control: no-store`. `revokeSessions` (default false) ends every session of the account in the `reset_link` mode; a temporary password ends them whatever it says. It works on an account of any rank that has a login: a guest is `409 NO_ACCOUNT` ("Make an account first."), an anonymized account `409 ANONYMIZED`, a suspended or blocked account `409 NOT_ACTIVE`. The link mode counts against five mails an hour per account (`429 RATE_LIMITED`). A temporary password works for 72 hours; after that it is refused like a wrong password and a new one must be set. Setting one also lifts the lock that repeated failed sign-ins put on the email.

post.description: The one way an account changes rank. Only the Owner may do it (`403 FORBIDDEN` otherwise), and the `Idempotency-Key` header is required (`422` without it): a retry with the same key and the same `groupId` answers the recorded change with the response header `idempotency-replayed: true`, another `groupId` under the key is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. The new rank must exist and differ from the current one (`422` on `groupId`). Inside one kind (merchant to merchant) only the rank changes, and a rank that allows no credit is refused while the credit limit is above zero (`409 RANK_CHANGE_BLOCKED`, code `credit_limit`). Across kinds the account must be free of everything that is still in flight: every reason found is listed together in `errors[]` on `groupId` with its code (`guest`, `open_hold`, `live_order`, `open_topup`, `open_dispute`, `open_refund`, `open_checkout`, `frozen`, `negative_balance`), and nothing is written. Otherwise the whole balance moves to the wallet of the new kind in one journal (kind `wallet_transfer`), the credit limit of a merchant wallet that is left is set to zero, every session of the account ends, every live API key is revoked when the account leaves the merchant kind, and an account without a password raised to a merchant rank is sent an invitation. The change and its blockers are audited. An anonymized account is `409 ANONYMIZED`.

post.description: Posts the manual adjustment (credit: Dr adjustments / Cr the wallet; debit: the mirror) with the reason in the memo, and audits it. It works on the live wallet of either kind. A staff member's credits to wallets of one kind within 24 hours, this one included and, for merchant wallets, counted with the parts by which they raised credit limits, above the approval limit of that kind (settings `wallet.adjust_approval_limit` for merchant wallets, default $10,000, and `wallet.customer.adjust_approval_limit` for store balances, default $500), or a single debit above it, are refused with `409 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; an Owner is not limited and a retry of an accepted adjustment is answered as before (decision 049). A merchant debit below the credit limit is `CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; a store debit below zero is `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`; a store credit needs an account that can sign in and is not anonymized (`NO_ACCOUNT`, `ANONYMIZED`) and mails the customer. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required for both kinds: a retry with the same key and body answers the first adjustment (`idempotency-replayed: true`), also for a store adjustment made before the accounts merged; the same key with another body is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Works while the wallet is on hold.

post.description: Puts the live wallet, of either kind, on hold. A merchant wallet on hold takes no new order hold (`409 WALLET_FROZEN`) and no credit-limit raise, while settlement and release of holds that exist, credits and staff debits still post; a store balance stops paying from the balance and card top-ups. Freezing a wallet that is on hold changes nothing (still audited). Audited; a store balance owner is emailed. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required: a retry with the same key and body answers the first result (`idempotency-replayed: true`), also after a later unfreeze, and changes nothing; the same key with another body is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

get.description: Landing pages (`kind` carrier, model, tool, brand, country) and content pages (`static`, `blog`) in one table. `kind` may repeat (`kind=static&kind=blog`). `q` is a contains over the title and the slug. Default order: last change first. The stats above the tables ask with `_start=0&_end=1`. Rows carry the full Markdown body.

parameters.name: _start
parameters.description: First row to return (0-based, inclusive). Default 0.

parameters.name: _end
parameters.description: Row after the last one to return (exclusive). Default _start + 25; a page holds at most 1000 rows.

parameters.name: _sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields. Allowed: updatedAt, title, status, createdAt, publishedAt, slug, id. Default: updatedAt desc.

parameters.name: _order
parameters.description: Comma-separated directions (asc or desc), one per sort field in the same order.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text search over: title, slug.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Keep rows where kind equals (repeat the key for IN) the value.

parameters.name: kind_ne
parameters.description: Keep rows where kind is not (repeat the key for NOT IN) the value.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keep rows where status equals (repeat the key for IN) the value.

parameters.name: status_ne

post.description: Makes a draft for each model x network: title `Unlock <model> on <network>`, slug from the title, kind `model`, status `draft`, `template_params` `{brand, model, network}` and a short body. Nothing is published. Empty lists mean everything the site knows: every brand of the TAC catalogue, every model (marketing name, else model) of those brands, every carrier of the service listings. A model that is not in the catalogue is generated when typed. Combinations that repeat an earlier one of the same run (the same slug) are merged; the distinct combinations whose slug already exists, or that a parallel run made first, are skipped and counted in `skipped`. A catalogue model with no Latin letter or digit cannot make a slug: it is left out and counted in `unusableModels` (present only when above 0), never a `422`; so is a listing carrier with no Latin letter or digit on a run with no networks typed, counted in `unusableNetworks` (present only when above 0). A run that would create more than 50 new drafts creates none: `422` with no field and the detail `This run would create N pages; the limit is 50 per run. Narrow the lists.`. A run over 20 000 combinations (a safety bound) is refused the same way, with N the number of combinations; so is a run with no models typed whose catalogue has more than 20 000 models (N is then 20001, where the read stops), whatever the networks. A typed model or network with no Latin letter or digit is `422` on `models` or `networks`. Needs `storefront:create` (B57). Audited as `generated landing pages`.

models.description: The models; one that the catalogue does not know is generated as typed. Empty means every model of those brands.

networks.description: The carriers, such as AT&T or Vodafone. Empty means every carrier of the service listings.

patch.description: Changes the fields sent. Sending `rateToBase` stamps the rate with the current time. The base currency USD refuses a new rate, a new markup and being switched off. The code cannot be changed once created. Audited. Sending `rateToBase`, `markupPercent` or `decimals` also needs `currencies:update` (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 046). A sent `rateToBase` also ends a hold of the refresh, and the shop offers the currency again (decision 049). A `rateToBase` more than `fx.max_refresh_move_percent` away from the stored rate (the comparison of the refresh: the larger over the smaller), or that far from the exchange-rate provider's rate when the provider offers the currency, needs an Owner: `403 FORBIDDEN` for anyone else, after the validation, and nothing in the patch is stored (decision 049). While an active storefront card payment method exists, `decimals` may not exceed what it can charge exactly (0 for whole-unit currencies such as JPY, else 2): `422` on `decimals` (`not_chargeable`, decision 048). Blocking sets the status `blocked`, ends every session, appends the reason to the internal notes, and adds to the blocklist, with source manual, the reason, the caller and the customer: the email, each distinct card fingerprint of their payments and each distinct IMEI still stored on their orders and checkouts (an entry that already exists is kept as it is and not linked to this customer). Unblocking sets `active` and deletes only the manual entries this customer’s block added. `reason` must be one of: Chargeback or dispute; Card testing or fraud; Abuse of refunds; Other (422 on `reason` otherwise). Audited as `blocked customer` or `unblocked customer`.

get.description: Retired with the one account type (decision 064): the route answers `410 ROUTE_RETIRED` and changes nothing; use `GET /admin/clients/:id/export`. What follows is the old behaviour, kept for a client that still calls it. A JSON file (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="customer-<id>.json"`, never cached) with everything the shop holds about the customer: the profile, the orders with their IMEI, the payments without card data, the consents, the checkout sessions, the support tickets with their public messages (only tickets whose requester's address is confirmed: a ticket opened on the contact form with a typed address is left out until its link is used), the data requests and the store balance with its statement (`wallet`, staff reasons hidden). It works for an anonymized customer too. The export closes the customer’s open or in-progress export request (`completed`, handled by the caller) and is audited as `exported data of`; no copy of the file is kept. Because a GET has this side effect and carries no CSRF token, the request must be started by the console itself (`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the console’s origins): anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED`.

post.description: Retired with the one account type (decision 064): the route answers `410 ROUTE_RETIRED` and changes nothing; use `POST /admin/clients/:id/password`. What follows is the old behaviour, kept for a client that still calls it. For an account only (`409 NO_ACCOUNT` for a guest). `mode` `reset_link` emails a new one-hour, single-use link and voids the older ones; `temporary_password` sets a generated 14-character password that the answer shows once and that must be changed at the first sign-in, and voids outstanding links; it also ends every session of the customer, whatever `revokeSessions` says, and sends the customer a security notice. `revokeSessions` ends every session of the customer in the link mode. The current password is never shown and never enters the audit log. A temporary password works for 72 hours; after that it is refused like a wrong password and a new one must be set. Setting one also lifts the lock that repeated failed sign-ins put on the email.

What follows is the old behaviour, kept for a client that still calls it. Posts a manual adjustment (credit: Dr adjustments / Cr customer_wallet; debit: the mirror) with the reason in the memo, audits it and emails the customer. A credit needs a customer with an account that is not anonymized (`NO_ACCOUNT`, `ANONYMIZED`); a debit never takes the balance below zero (`INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`). A staff member's credits to customer balances within 24 hours, this one included, above the approval limit (setting `wallet.customer.adjust_approval_limit`, default $500), or a single debit above it, are refused with `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; an Owner is not limited (decision 049). The `Idempotency-Key` header is required: a retry with the same key and body answers the first adjustment; the same key with another body is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Works while the balance is switched off or frozen.

get.description: One object, every section from one snapshot, cached about 15 seconds per (`scope`, `days`) (the sidebar reads it every minute for its counts). `scope` is `all`, `b2b` (the orders of the merchant doors) or `b2c` (the orders of the shop's door, `source` `store`); `days` is 1, 7 or 14. `stats` covers orders created in the rolling window; `previous` is the window of the same length before it, or `null` when it had no order. `attention` is every item ranked critical, high, medium, low (stable): `supplier_down` and `supplier_degraded` come only from a real down or degraded check, never from an unknown or missing one, and supplier items only for active suppliers. Each kind has its own fixed severity (RULES dashboard 3): `disputes_due` counts every dispute that needs a response and is critical when the first is due within 3 days; `orders_review` counts merchant-door orders only (a held storefront order is `orders_held`); `wallets_negative` lists accounts (the key stays `clients`) with a negative wallet of either kind: the merchant wallets for `b2b`, the store balances for `b2c`, both for `all`; `fx_stale` uses the currencies page rule (older than 24 hours). `queues` has one row per service type; `pastSla` is the one age-only rule shared with `GET /admin/orders?pastSla=true`. `suppliers` maps the latest check to `up`, `degraded`, `down`; a supplier with no check or no recent calls (an `unknown` check) is idle, neither healthy nor failing, and reads `unknown` (B180; the console shows "No recent calls"). `services_below_floor` is judged on the effective cost (user rule 9). Money is USD as a 4-decimal string; payments, refunds and disputes convert per row at the checkout's locked rate or the current currency rate and the sum is rounded once. `storefront` is `null` for `b2b`, `revenueByChannel` is `null` unless `scope=all`; the best buyers are not part of this answer (`GET /admin/reports/top-clients` ranks every account); `storefront` always covers the last 30 days and its funnel is the customers module's `storefrontFunnel(30)`.

post.description: Accepts the loss: the dispute is `lost` with `resolvedAt`, the payment `chargeback`, and one `b2c_chargeback` journal posts the amount and the dispute fee (Dr chargeback_loss, Cr gateway_clearing, key `dispute:<id>:chargeback`), kept in `disputes.ledger_tx_id` so a later `lost` event from the gateway posts nothing again. For an order that was never delivered (`rejected`) the journal gives back what the sale booked as owed to the buyer and as VAT for the disputed share of what the refunds that went out left (Dr customer_funds, Dr vat_payable), and only the rest and the dispute fee go to chargeback_loss. Refunds of the payment the gateway has not paid (requested, waiting to be sent, or failed) are closed `rejected` with the note "Not sent: the payment was charged back." and their journals reversed, so the money leaves the books once (decision 048). The customer is not blocked (M115). `409 DISPUTE_NOT_OPEN` when it no longer waits for evidence.

get.description: Redirects (`302`) to a presigned object-storage link that expires after 5 minutes (`Content-Disposition: attachment` with the stored file name, `Cache-Control: no-store`). `:id` is `orders.inputFileId`, `result.fileId` of an order, an identity document stored before the document check was retired, a payment receipt, an invoice PDF, dispute evidence or a ticket attachment. Besides `files:read` the caller needs the read permission of every record that uses the file: `clients:read` (an identity document stored earlier), `payments:read` (a payment receipt), `disputes:read` (dispute evidence), `orders:read` (an order’s input or result), `invoices:read` (an invoice PDF), `support:read` (a ticket attachment), `customers:privacy` (a data export); `403 FORBIDDEN` names the first one missing. A file nothing uses yet needs `clients:read` when an account uploaded it (every rank), and a public picture needs only `files:read`. Every download of an identity document or a payment receipt writes an audit row (decision 047). The console renders a plain link, so an error is shown raw in the new tab: the `detail` is readable.

post.description: A storefront payment the gateway confirmed that could not pay its checkout is held for staff (decision 048): it has no order, and the money integrity check lists it until its money is back. `returned`: staff paid it back by hand (at the gateway or by transfer); a completed refund without an order records it, and a later confirmation of the payment changes nothing. `not_received`: the gateway holds no money for it; the payment becomes `failed` (a later real confirmation can still pay its checkout). `not_received` is accepted only when the gateway's record did not show money received for the payment when it was held (not paid, could not be checked, or the record of another checkout); a payment whose record showed its money received (another amount or currency, no checkout, money refunded or disputed since) is `409 CONFLICT` ("The gateway's record shows this payment was received: send it back, then close it as returned."), and a payment held before this rule accepts both outcomes. `note` (10 to 500 characters) says what staff did. A payment that is not held, or whose money is being sent back or was sent back, is `409 CONFLICT`; an unknown id or a top-up is `404`. Audited.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change. A new `status`, or a non-empty `update` (at most 1000 characters), appends one timeline line {now, status, `update` or a default sentence, the staff member}. `status: "resolved"` closes the incident: it needs a `rootCause` of at least 10 characters (sent now, or saved earlier), sets `resolvedAt` and `resolvedBy`, and the optional `update` ("the action taken") becomes the `resolved` line (B104). A resolved incident cannot be changed or reopened: `409 INCIDENT_CLOSED`. Writes the audit entry `updated incident` (`closed incident` when it closes).

post.description: An allow rule is always for the admin console (the scope is forced to `admin`). A block needs a `reason`. `cidr` is an address or a range of at least /16 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) with no bits set after the prefix. A live rule with the same range and kind (and, for blocks, scope) is refused. A block of the admin console or of everything that covers the caller's own address is `409 SELF_LOCKOUT`. The rule cache is cleared after the commit. A caller who is not an owner gets `403 FORBIDDEN` for a block of the admin console or of everything that would shut out an address an active owner uses: an address of a live owner session, or an active owner's last sign-in address (decision 046). The change is judged as things are and at each later moment a rule runs out: an owner's address may not be refused at any moment at which it would have been allowed without the change.

post.description: Adds a template for an event, channel and audience. The event must be registered for the audience (`event` is 422 otherwise) and offer the channel; the placeholders of the subject and body come only from the event’s variables (422 on `subject` or `body`); an email needs a subject. One template per event, channel and audience (templates have no language, B226): a second one is 422 on `event`. For an email whose `{{link}}` is a one-time credential (the sign-in, password, invitation and verification links, the ticket links, the checkout reminder) the subject cannot hold `{{link}}`, and the body uses it only on its own (at the start of a line or after a space) or as the whole `href` of one link with a text, holds no other web address, and uses only text formatting tags (422 on `subject` or `body`, codes `link_*`; decision 047). The markup must be read the same way by the text part of the email: an attribute value holds no character reference outside the short list the check decodes, no `<`, `>`, double quote or the word `href`, an end tag closes with `>` right after its name, and a lone `<` in an HTML message is written `<`. An email that protects accounts keeps `{{link}}` (or, for a security notice, `{{change}}`) in the text of its body, outside every tag, attribute and comment (422 on `body`, code `security_placeholder`; decision 047); the body of every such email, a notice included, is also checked for comments, declarations and tags outside the list, refuses a `style` or `hidden` attribute (`link_*` codes), and the body of a notice holds no `href`. Writes the audit entry `created notification template`.

post.description: Points the order at another supplier (`supplierId`: the supplier's id; its active link of the order's service with the lowest priority gives the supplier service) and/or forgets the old reference (`resetReference`). Nothing is sent to the supplier. `unit_cost` and `total_cost` are refreshed from the chosen link (`credit x credit_rate`; the price stays); a costlier link is allowed for staff and the `supplier_changed` event records `costAbovePrice`. Choosing another supplier always forgets the old reference. The dispatch state stays, except a `sent` order whose reference is forgotten, which becomes `needs_attention`; with `dispatch: true` it becomes `pending` and the job is queued in the same transaction. Neither `supplierId` nor `resetReference: true` is `422` on `supplierId`; the same supplier without a reset is a `204` with no event. An order being sent to its supplier right now is `409 ALREADY_SENT`; `dispatch: true` for a storefront order whose payment is disputed, charged back or refunded in full is `409 INVALID_TRANSITION`.

post.description: Staff retry: an order in `needs_attention`, `manual` or `operator` goes to `pending` and the dispatch job is queued (an `order.dispatch_requested` outbox row; the answer does not wait for the supplier). The order goes to the supplier service it already has, else the first active link whose supplier is active; the price-protection limit of the automatic dispatch does not apply. No money moves: the hold stays. An order already `pending` whose dispatch request is still waiting for the job is a `204` that changes nothing; one whose request was lost gets a new one (a `retry` event, the job queued) and keeps its supplier columns: the job chooses the target by the automatic rule. An order being sent to its supplier right now is `409 ALREADY_SENT`. A storefront order whose payment is disputed, charged back or refunded in full is `409 INVALID_TRANSITION` (the order stays where it is). Writes a `retry` event and an audit row.

post.description: Rejects an open order with a buyer-visible reason: `result_code` is the reason, `completed_at` is set and the hold returns to the wallet (B2B `reject`). Writes `rejected` and `release` events, `order.status_changed` and an audit row. A storefront order delivered before and then reopened is refunded from the Refunds page (`USE_REFUNDS`). While the order is being sent to its supplier the action waits for the answer: `409 ALREADY_SENT`. Rejecting an open storefront order that has a captured payment gives the payment back, so it also needs `refunds:approve` (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 046). The payment of a storefront order goes back to the buyer at once, except a payment the buyer disputed with the card network (decision 048): while it is `disputed` nothing is sent, a refund request waits on the Refunds page and the order’s timeline says why; once it is `chargeback` the card network has returned the money, so no refund or request is made, what the sale booked as customer funds and VAT goes back against the chargeback loss once (a `chargeback` journal on the order) and the timeline says so.

post.description: Sends a completed order back to `processing` (dispatch state `operator`, no queue): `completed_at` and the result are cleared and the settled revenue returns to the hold (a reversing entry; the cost stays booked). Writes a `reopened` event, `order.status_changed` and an audit row. A later reply settles it again. A reopen moves revenue back to the merchant hold, which is a new debit and not a refund: when the buyer account no longer has a merchant rank (the live wallet is the store balance) it is `409 RANK_CHANGED` ("Refund the order instead."), and nothing is posted. An erased account (anonymized) is `409 ANONYMIZED`.

post.description: Completes an open order: `result_code` and `result_comment` are stored, `completed_at` is set, `dispatch_state` becomes `done`. The hold is settled to revenue (B2B `complete`: hold to revenue, plus supplier prepaid to cost of goods only when a supplier executed the order and no earlier settlement booked the cost). Writes `completed` and `settle` events, `order.status_changed` and an audit row. Two parallel replies, or a reply and a reject, change the order and the ledger once: the other answers `409`. While the order is being sent to its supplier the action waits for the answer: `409 ALREADY_SENT`. A storefront order whose payment is disputed, charged back or refunded in full is not completed by staff: `409 INVALID_TRANSITION` with a sentence that names the reason (a reject stays allowed). One that was delivered before and reopened is delivered again.

patch.description: Changes the fields sent (the on/off switch sends `{ isActive }`). The code never changes (it is part of the webhook address): a different code is 422 on `code`. A non-empty `secret` or `webhookSecret` replaces the stored one; leaving it out keeps it. `secondaryWebhookSecret` sets the second webhook secret, `null` removes it, leaving it out keeps it. A `preset` in the body is ignored: the preset of a method never changes, and a method made from one keeps its kind and driver: a merged `isManual` that is not the preset kind is 422 on `isManual` (`preset_kind`), a merged `driver` that is not the preset driver is 422 on `driver` (`preset_driver`). A custom method may still change both. The merged gateway is validated as on create. Validation (422 with the field): a non-blank name, driver and code (lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_`); a code that no other gateway uses; audience b2c, b2b or both; a fee of 0 to 100 percent; money fields of 0 or more (a maximum above zero is not below the minimum); whole `holdHours` from 0 to 720; `allowedGroupIds` that are existing client groups; a `secondaryWebhookSecret` of 1 to 500 characters, only next to a first webhook secret. Audited. Only an owner may send `secret`, `webhookSecret` or `secondaryWebhookSecret` (a `null` for a method that has no second secret changes nothing and is open to the route's own permission), change `isManual` of a method that is automatic before or after the change (turning an automatic method manual included), or change the `driver` of such a method (`403 FORBIDDEN`, after the validation; decision 046). post.description: Approves a top-up and credits the wallet in one transaction: the money event `deposit` (Dr bank for a manual gateway or gateway_clearing for an automatic one, Cr client_wallet net, Cr fee_income fee, idempotency key `deposit:payment:<id>`), the linked invoice becomes paid, `invoice.paid` is queued for the merchant notification, and the decision is audited. Only a pending top-up can be decided, and only when its gateway is manual or the payment was sent to review (`409 PAYMENT_AUTO_CREDIT_PENDING` otherwise: an automatic gateway credits by itself after the gateway check). A decided payment is `409 PAYMENT_ALREADY_REVIEWED`. An order (storefront) payment is `404`. Approving is `409 CONFLICT` when the gateway confirmed another amount or currency than the invoice (reject it and adjust the wallet by hand), when the gateway event can no longer be read, or when the invoice is no longer open. The answer's `client.walletBalance` already includes the credit. `403 FORBIDDEN` when the payment pays a manual invoice the caller issued, unless the caller is an Owner (decision 049). A top-up that a merchant or customer made through a manual method whose credit takes what the caller approved of such top-ups within 24 hours above `wallet.receipt_approval_limit` (default $10,000) is `409 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` and nothing is posted; an Owner is not limited (decision 049).

post.description: Rejects a top-up with the reason the merchant sees: the payment becomes rejected with the reason as its note, the linked top-up invoice is voided (a staff-issued manual invoice stays open: the merchant may upload another receipt), nothing is posted to the ledger, and the decision is audited. post.description: Starts a draft of the services of a scope to put on the shop: `services` (1 to 500 ids the staff member ticked), `category`, `supplier` (live services linked to a service of it), `quickAddRun` (the services that Quick add run created), `run` (an earlier publish run: a draft, which "Check again" replaces, or the rest of a finished one) or `all`. `listed` (default `true`; for the scope `run` the old run's) says whether apply switches the listings on. The rows of a run are the live services of the scope that have no listing; with `services` a ticked service that has a listing is a row too (`blocked`, `already_listed`). Answers `202` with the run in `preparing`, `total` the services counted now; the worker names and evaluates every row and closes it as a `draft`. A preview changes nothing a visitor or a merchant can see. `422` on `scope`: `nothing_to_publish` (no service left to publish, also when every ticked service has a listing) and `too_many` (more than 5000); `422` with the code `invalid` on `scope.categoryId`, `scope.supplierId` or `scope.runId` for an unknown one. The scope `run` answers `409 CONFLICT` for a run that is still working, for one whose preview was never finished (its rows are partial), and for a draft that "Check again" replaced while the newer run is alive or was prepared. When the newer run died before its preview was ready, the same request ("Prepare again") copies the old draft again, and the draft links to the new run. "Check again" from a draft cancels that draft in the same transaction. audit: false for the draft itself (a draft is not a record of the shop; apply, cancel and the run switch are audited); the one audit row is the `cancelled publishing run` of the draft that "Check again" replaces.

post.description: Starts publishing the ticked rows of a draft (`202`, the run is `queued`; a worker publishes one service per transaction). `listed` says whether the listings go on the shop (left out: the run's own choice). A run that `failed`, or that was `queued` or `running` and stalled (five minutes without a heartbeat), whose draft was prepared, **resumes**: rows with a result stay, rows that failed unexpectedly are tried again, the rest continues, and a run switch that stalled is closed as `failed`. `422` on `included` with the code `nothing_included` when a draft has no ticked row. `409 JOB_ALREADY_RUNNING` when the run (or its switch) is being worked on. `409 CONFLICT` when the preview is still being prepared or was never finished (start a new one), or the run is finished. One transaction takes the run row `FOR UPDATE`, so a row in flight finishes first and an edit of the draft after it answers `409`. Audited (`started publishing to the storefront`).

post.summary: Change many rows of a publish draft

patch.description: Changes one row of a draft and judges it again on the service as it is now (`200` with the row). Keys: `title` (1 to 200, one line), `slug` (an address, or an empty text to make it from the title again; an address that is not typed follows an edited title), `brand` and `carrier` (at most 80), `country` (two letters or empty), `retailPrice` (a typed price), `pricing` (`rule` or `keep`), `included` (the tick) and `reset` (back to what was detected, alone in the body). At least one key. A row that the new facts block (the service was disabled since, a typed price under a floor that rose) is stored `blocked` and unticked, with `200`. `403` naming `pricing:update` when the body carries `retailPrice` or `pricing`, or `reset` on a row that holds a typed price or a rule chosen over a typed price, and the role lacks it. `409` when the run is no longer a draft, or the service is gone. `422`: `retailPrice` `invalid` (zero or less) or `below_floor` ("Below the storefront floor of $X."); `slug` `invalid` or `duplicate` (a listing or another row holds it); `pricing` `invalid` (`keep` on a service with no retail price); `included` `blocked` (the row is blocked after the change: the sentence names the reason); `retailPrice` beside `pricing`, or `reset` beside anything, with the code `conflict`. One transaction takes the run row `FOR SHARE` and checks the `draft` under it, then the row `FOR UPDATE`, so an edit and an apply never interleave. audit: false: a draft is not a record of the shop; apply, cancel and the run switch are audited. A price needs the permission it needs on the listing route (decision 046).

post.description: Takes every listing the run published off the shop (`listed: false`), or puts it back (`listed: true`); `202`, with `switch.status` `queued`, and a worker does it. Nothing is deleted and no price changes: a listing whose service was disabled meanwhile, or whose price was removed, is left as it is when switching on. Allowed for a `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled` run that published something, and again after a switch that is `done`, `failed` or stalled; a `queued` or `running` run that stalled is first closed `failed` by this request. `409 CONFLICT` when the run is not finished or published nothing; `409 JOB_ALREADY_RUNNING` when a switch is being worked on. Audited (`started switching publishing run`).

The buyer is an account of any rank, a guest included, and a refund goes back to the wallet the account holds now (decision 064). Newest first. The page counts of the console are this call with `_start=0&_end=1` and a `status` filter. `q` searches the id, the reason and the account name and email (a guest has only an email); the email only for callers who hold `clients:read` (decision 047). post.description: Approves a waiting refund in full or in part and posts its journal once (`b2c_refund`, key `refund:<id>`): a delivered order is reversed from revenue (the supplier cost is never recovered), an order that was not delivered is cancelled and refunded in full from customer funds; the VAT share is `round(tax x amount / paid, 2)`. A card or wallet refund goes to the gateway through a job (`processing` until it answers, then `completed` or `failed`); a crypto payment, or a gateway that cannot refund, is paid out by hand and is `completed` at once. A payment made from the balance goes back to the wallet the account holds now (the store balance, or the merchant wallet after a rank change, decision 064), with the same key and the same limit; for an erased account (anonymized) it is `409 ANONYMIZED` and nothing changes (nobody can open that wallet: pay it back another way and decline the request). Without `amount` the amount on the request is refunded; the limit is what was paid minus the other refunds that are completed or processing. The answer carries `netAmount` and `taxAmount` of the posted journal. An order that is being sent to its supplier right now is `409 ALREADY_SENT` (approve it once the supplier answered).

amount.description: A USD amount with up to 4 decimals (`7.5000`); left out means the amount on the request.

get.description: A PDF (`application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="statement-<clientId>-<from>-<to>.pdf"` with the UTF-8 form, `Cache-Control: no-store`) made on the spot from the ledger, not stored. It is the statement of the live wallet (decision 064): the merchant wallet of a merchant rank, the store balance of the retail rank. It shows the account (name, company, country), the period, the opening balance, the wallet lines oldest first (date, `JRN-<id>`, kind, memo, debit, credit, balance after), the totals, the closing balance, the credit limit (merchant wallet only) and the invoices of that wallet issued in the period (the top-ups of a store balance). Amounts are USD with 4 decimals. `from` and `to` are UTC days, both included; the default is the whole history (from the day of the first wallet line to today). Lines are ordered by ledger entry id, so the closing balance is the wallet balance. Without `from`, a history of more than 10,000 lines is cut to the most recent 10,000 and the period starts on the day of the first of them (the opening balance is the balance before that line), and a history of more than 10,000 invoices is cut to the newest 10,000 the same way; only an explicit `from` period with more than 10,000 lines, or with more than 10,000 invoices, is `422`. Every download writes an audit row (`exported statement of`). It is answered only to a request started by the console itself (`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the console’s origins); anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED` and writes no audit row. It also needs `wallet:read`, as the wallet statement does (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 046).

Rejects the order without contacting a supplier and returns the whole payment (the storefront refund ledger move), in one transaction with the assessment outcome, the order timeline, the audit row and the chosen blocklist entries (manual entries of the caller; an entry that already exists is skipped, and none is linked to an account). The account’s status is not changed: block the account with `POST /admin/clients/:id/block`. `409 NOT_HELD` when the order is not waiting for a decision any more. A payment the buyer disputed with the card network is not sent back (decision 048): while the dispute is open a refund request waits on the Refunds page instead; once the payment was charged back no refund or request is made and what the sale booked goes back against the chargeback loss. For a guest checkout (opened without a signed-in session) `blockEmail` also blocks the card that paid the order, and blocks the checkout’s email for guest checkouts only when that email belonged to an account before the order: the account keeps signing in and ordering signed in, and its status is never changed here (decision 050).

patch.description: Any of the fields below; at least one. `isListed` and `retailPrice` (4-decimal net USD before VAT) work as before: `retailPrice` writes the retail group price of the service, so it applies only to new storefront checkouts; a price of zero or less, or under `floorPrice`, is `422` on `retailPrice` ("Below the storefront floor of $X."); a typed price stops the price following a rule. `retailPricing: "rule"` writes the price the retail price rule of the service gives now and makes it follow the rule from then on (decision 040); it is `422` on `retailPricing` with the code `conflict` when `retailPrice` is sent too, `no_rule` when no active rule covers the service, `no_cost` when the service has no cost, and `409 LISTING_LOCKED` as for a price. Switching a disabled service on is `409 SERVICE_DISABLED`; switching on or pricing a service that can never be public is `409 LISTING_LOCKED`. Switching off is always allowed. Switching on for the first time sets `listedAt`; it never resets. Content: `publicTitle`, `slug` (a form that is not lower-case words joined by hyphens is `422` on `slug`; one used by another listing is `409 LISTING_EXISTS` on `slug`; changing it changes the public link), `summary`, `descriptionMd`, `requirementsMd`, `etaText`, `seoTitle`, `seoDescription`, `brand`, `carrier`, `country` (empty or two letters), `isFeatured`, `sort`. Every refusal is decided before the first write. Each change is audited (`listed on storefront`, `unlisted from storefront`, `changed retail price of`, `edited listing of`; the audit row keeps the length of the Markdown bodies, not their text). Every row also says whether its price follows a rule (`retailPriceSource`, `retailPriceRule`, `retailPriceWaiting`). Besides `storefront:update`: switching a listing on (`isListed` true while it is off) also needs `storefront:publish`; `retailPrice` and `retailPricing` also need `pricing:update` (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 046).

post.description: `multipart/form-data` with one part named `file`: a JPEG, PNG or WebP picture, at most 2 MiB, 200 to 4096 pixels on each side. The type is read from the content (the declared type and the file name are ignored). The picture is cleaned before it is stored (EXIF, XMP, IPTC, comments and text chunks are removed, anything after the end of the picture is cut) and stored once under the SHA-256 of the cleaned bytes. It becomes the picture of the service (replacing the previous one) and the `imageUrl` of the answer and of the public service cards. Refusals are `422` on `file` with the code: `empty`, `unsupported_type`, `corrupt`, `animated`, `too_small`, `too_large_dimensions`, `rotated` (a JPEG whose EXIF turns it: save it upright); more than 2 MiB is `413`. A JSON or form body has no file part, so it is `422` on `file`; a body of a type the API does not read is `415`. A multipart body is read only with a live staff session. Audited (`uploaded image for`).

post.description: Starts `active`, `auto`, with a fixed price mode, the `block_open` duplicate rule, no minimum profit of its own and a cost of 0 until a supplier is linked or imported. The type must be the type of the category: `422` on `categoryId` otherwise. A code that another live service has (ignoring case) is `409 CODE_TAKEN` on `code`. `basePrice` must be above zero. The optional `allowCancel`, `allowVerify` and `verifyWindowH` (0 to 720 hours, `0` = no window) switch on the merchant's cancel and verification of this service's orders; all three start off. The optional `minQty`, `maxQty` (whole, 1 to 100000) and `qtyOptions` (at most 50 whole pack sizes, no repeats) say what one order may buy; they start at 1, 1 and none. A service sells a range or packs: with `qtyOptions` the server stores `minQty` as the smallest and `maxQty` as the largest pack and refuses a different one sent (`422` `packs_set`); without packs a `maxQty` under `minQty` is `422` `below_min` on `maxQty` (`above_max` on `minQty` when only `minQty` was sent). Every pack problem (`invalid_pack`, `duplicate_pack`) is on `qtyOptions`. The values are in the audit row `created service`.

post.description: Sets the position (`sort`) of 1 to 500 services in one transaction: either every position is saved or none is. A position is a whole number from 0 to 1000000; merchants and API clients read services by category position, then this number, then the name, so services with the same number stay in name order. A service already at its position is left alone. A service that is listed twice, or is unknown or archived, is `422` on `items.N.id` (N the later of two equal ids; every problem comes back together) and nothing is saved. The answer says how many services changed. One audit entry (`changed the order of`) holds the old and new positions of the changed services (the first 200), the cached merchant price lists start over, and the services are locked in id order, so two saves never interleave.

patch.description: Only the keys sent change. Saving `basePrice` clears `costChangedFrom`; a `minProfit`-only change does not; `minProfit: null` goes back to the default policy. A `basePrice` under the floor (effective cost plus the minimum profit being saved) or not above zero is `422` on `basePrice`. The category and type must agree (`422` on `categoryId`, or on `type` when only the type was sent). A code another live service has is `409 CODE_TAKEN`. `allowCancel`, `allowVerify` and `verifyWindowH` (0 to 720 hours, `0` = no window) set what a merchant may do with this service's orders. `minQty`, `maxQty` and `qtyOptions` set what one order may buy; a key left out keeps its stored value, and when any of them is sent the whole rule is checked again (the same refusals as on create: `below_min`, `above_max`, `invalid_pack`, `duplicate_pack`, `packs_set`, all `422`). Packs are stored ascending and set `minQty` and `maxQty` to the smallest and largest pack. `qtyOptions: []` clears the packs; the service then sells the range `minQty..maxQty`, so send both in the same request (left out, the stored ones, the former smallest and largest pack, stay). Example body: `{ "qtyOptions": [5, 10, 25] }`. The audit row `edited service` holds the three values before and after. Sending `basePrice` or `minProfit` also needs `pricing:update` (`403 FORBIDDEN`, decision 046).

put.description: The whole list in order (the index is the sort order); a field left out is deleted. One transaction. A row may carry the `key` of a field the service has (that is how a saved field is recognised and keeps its key for ever); a row without a key is a new field and the server makes its key from the name (lower snake case, `_2`, `_3` on a clash, `field` when nothing is left). The name is what a supplier receives in `CUSTOMFIELD`. `label` left out keeps the saved label of an existing field, an empty label stores the name, and a new field without a label gets the name. `isMainInput` left out keeps the saved value of an existing field and is `false` for a new one. On an IMEI service a list that leaves no field as the main input makes the first field named IMEI (any letter case) the main input. An unknown field type, an empty name or a pattern outside the supported form (decision 051: literals, classes, the escapes `\d \w \s` and their capitals, groups that neither repeat nor nest, counts up to 500, `^` and `$` at the ends, and a bound on the work of a 500-character value) is `422` on `fields.N.<name>`; so are an unknown or repeated key (`fields.N.key`), a name that an earlier field already has, ignoring letter case (`fields.N.name`), and a second main input (`fields.N.isMainInput`). An unknown or archived service is `404`.

put.description: The whole set, including the storefront retail group (`b2c_retail`); a group left out loses its fixed price (it then pays the base price less its discount). One transaction, answers the saved prices by group id. Every row must be at or above its floor, rows kept unchanged included: a merchant group row at the effective cost plus the minimum profit for that group (`422` on `prices.N.price`, "Below the floor of $X (cost $Y plus $Z minimum profit)."), the retail row at the storefront floor `max(round(base price x 1.10, 2), floor)` ("Below the storefront floor of $X."). A group listed twice is `422` on `prices.N.groupId` ("Listed twice", the later row); an unknown group is `422` on `prices.N.groupId`; a price not above zero is `422` on `prices.N.price`. An unknown or archived service is `404`. `retailPriceSeen` is the retail price the form loaded (`null`: it loaded none): when the retail row sent is that same figure (or absent, for `null`), nobody changed it, so the retail price stored now stays as it is and keeps following its rule, even if it moved since the form opened, and the row sent is neither written nor held to the floor. Without the key every row counts as sent.

get.description: A server-sent event stream (`text/event-stream`) of the signed-in person (a staff member or an account): `ready` first, `hb` every 15 seconds, `notification.created`, `notification.read`, `unread.changed`, `resync` and `bye`; the data of every event is one line of JSON (docs/contract/realtime-events.md). A reconnect sends the last event id back (`Last-Event-ID`, or `cursor`) and gets what it missed, at most 50 items, else `resync`. At most 3 streams per session and 30 per address (429 for the next one), ended after 15 minutes (`bye max_age`) and when the session ends (`bye session_ended`). Only a request started by the page’s own site is answered: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the origins of the route’s audience (the console’s for `/admin`, the shop’s for `/client` and `/store/v1`); anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED`. A refusal is an ordinary problem+json answer before the stream starts. `503 UNAVAILABLE` when live updates are switched off or the server is full: keep polling.

A change of `status` recomputes the effective cost of the services linked to the supplier (it follows the first link an order can use) and moves the catalog price version.

post.description: A new item becomes a service: type from the supplier's type (`imei`, `server`, `remote` or `file`, else `422` on `supplierServiceIds` naming it and nothing is imported), the category found or created from the supplier's group (`Imported` when empty), automatic fulfilment, code `IMP-<id>` (`-2`, `-3` on a collision), the SLA read from the supplier's time text (the setting `catalog.importDefaultSlaMinutes`, default 1440, when it cannot be read), the suggested price, the supplier's custom fields and a link of priority 1. A changed item updates the linked service's cost and recomputes its effective cost (price untouched; an archived service counts as unchanged). Ids of another supplier are ignored. `createdServiceIds` names the services this call created, in creation order (decision 060). Two optional keys change only what a new item becomes (decision 063): `status` (`active`, the default, or `disabled`: the service is inserted disabled, in the same transaction, so it is never orderable) and `categoryId` (the category every new service goes into instead of the one named after the supplier's group; it must have the type of each new service, else `422` on `categoryId` naming the supplier services that do not fit, and nothing is imported; an unknown id is `422` on `categoryId` too). An updated or unchanged item is not touched by either. Without the keys the route is what it was.

post.description: For each picked service of this supplier: `new` (no service links it), `matching` (linked, and the service cost equals `credit x credit_rate`) or `changed` (linked, the cost differs: `previousCost` is the service's current cost). `suggestedPrice` (new and changed) is the cost plus the default minimum profit. `minQty`, `maxQty` and `qtyOptions` are the supplier's quantity rule as the import reads it (a Dhru supplier's QNT, MINQNT, MAXQNT and QNTOPTIONS; unreadable values mean one per order): for a `new` item, what the service will get. `quantityDiffers` is true when the item is linked to a live service whose own rule is another one; the service keeps its own rule, and staff edit it to follow the supplier. Changes nothing, so it writes no audit row. With `status` or `categoryId` (decision 063, the keys of the import) every item also says the `status` and the `category` a `new` item would get: `status` is `active` unless asked, `category` the picked one, else the category the import finds for the supplier's group, else the name it makes one under with `id` `null`; both are `null` for an item the import would not create. A `categoryId` of another type than a new item answers the import's `422` on `categoryId`. Without either key the items carry neither.

post.description: Adds the supplier's services to the catalog in the background, by whole group or all of them. Body `{ scope: 'all' }` or `{ scope: 'groups', groups: [{ type, remoteGroup }] }` (1 to 500 groups, compared exactly with the stored text; exact repeats are dropped), and `serviceStatus` (`active` by default, or `disabled` to add them switched off). The client never sends ids: the server takes only the candidates of the scope, the services that are not in the console yet, are still available and have an importable type, and counts the rest as left out. It only creates (the picker import's rules: category by type and group, suggested price, fields, quantity rule); a service already in the console is never changed. Answers `202` with the run in `queued`; the worker adds the services in chunks and the run's `processed` moves. A supplier has one live run: a second start answers `409 JOB_ALREADY_RUNNING` (unless the live run stalled: it is closed and a new one starts); a `disabled` supplier answers `409 SUPPLIER_DISABLED` (a paused one is accepted). A scope with no candidate answers `422` on `scope` with code `nothing_to_add` and creates no run. With `publish: { listed }` the run also puts what it creates on the shop when it ends: the services are handed to the bulk publish, which prepares a preview and publishes the ready rows at the retail pricing rules' prices (the ones that need a person wait in Storefront, Publish). `publish` answers `403 FORBIDDEN` naming `storefront:publish` when the staff member lacks it, `422` on `publish` with code `needs_active` when `serviceStatus` is `disabled`, and code `no_rule` when no retail price rule is active. Writes the audit row `started quick add from`; the worker writes `quick added services from` when the run ends. The publish run is found with `GET /admin/publish-runs?quickAddRunId=<run id>`.

post.description: Runs the supplier-sync job (the worker calls `imeiservicelist` and `accountinfo`) and answers its counts. The API waits up to `timeoutMs` + 5 s: a supplier failure is `409 SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE`; a wait that runs out while the job goes on is `504 SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT`. A paused supplier may sync; a disabled one is `409 SUPPLIER_DISABLED`. A supplier whose `accountinfo` reports another currency than its own is `409 SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is saved. The sync updates `supplier_services` (a changed credit sets `price_changed_at`; a service no longer listed becomes unavailable), recomputes the effective cost of every linked service and moves the catalog price version. It also adopts the supplier's main box (decision 042): an IMEI service whose only active link points at a service of this supplier whose main box asks for something other than an IMEI (an ECID, a serial number) becomes a server service with that box as its first field. On every service whose only active link points at this supplier it also makes required the fields the supplier requires (a Dhru Fusion site writes `"required": "on"`) that were imported as optional; it never makes a field optional. `adopted` counts the services brought in line, each once. A service whose price cannot be read or is outside 0 to 1000000000 is left out (unavailable until the supplier lists it with a usable price); a balance outside -1000000000 to 1000000000 is not saved: the sync goes on and answers the stored balance and its time (the sync's time when none was ever stored). Both are counted in a warning of the log (decision 051).

get.description: The five checks of the last finished run of the job `ledger_integrity` (nightly at 02:30 UTC and manual): every entry sums to zero, every account balance equals the sum of its lines (the same comparison as `POST /admin/ledger/reconcile`, debit-positive differences), no hold of a merchant-door order is stuck for more than 24 hours, every confirmed payment has an entry, and every wallet follows the rank of its account (`wallets_follow_rank`, findings of kind `account`): a wallet of the kind the rank does not use holds money, carries a credit limit or is on hold, a merchant wallet has a credit limit on a rank without credit, or a ledger account has no account behind it. Each check has a `status`, the full `count`, the summed `difference` and the first 20 findings with a label, a reference and, where it applies, the difference, the age or the time of the last entry. A check reads `unknown` when it never ran (a run made before the fifth check existed shows it unknown). The check only reads the ledger: a difference is put right with a reversing entry in Finance. During a database outage the route answers `503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`.

post.description: The Dhru Fusion v6.1 compatible endpoint (decision 026): `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object) as a form body (`multipart/form-data` and JSON are accepted too). Eight actions: `accountinfo`, `imeiservicelist`, `placeimeiorder`, `placeimeiorderbulk`, `getimeiorder`, `getimeiorderbulk`, `placefileorder` and `getfileorder`. Every answer is HTTP 200 with the headers `X-Powered-By: DHRU-FUSION` and `dhru-fusion-api-version: 6.1` and the body `{ "SUCCESS": [ ... ], "apiversion": "6.1" }` or `{ "ERROR": [ { "MESSAGE": "..." } ], "apiversion": "6.1" }`; a bulk action answers `{ "<request id>": { "SUCCESS" | "ERROR": [ ... ] }, ..., "apiversion": "6.1" }`. A wrong credential is "Authentication Failed", an unknown action "Invalid Action". The allowed addresses and the per-minute limit of the key apply. A text in the decoded `parameters` or `CUSTOMFIELD` may not hold the character U+0000 or an unpaired surrogate.

oneOf.title: accountinfo
oneOf.description: Account info. The merchant's available balance (`credit`: the wallet balance plus the credit limit), email and currency. The key `AccoutInfo` is spelled as in the Dhru Fusion standard.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: This action takes no parameters.

credit.description: What the merchant may spend now: balance plus credit limit.

oneOf.title: imeiservicelist
oneOf.description: IMEI service list. The IMEI, server and remote services the merchant may order, grouped by category, at its own price (`CREDIT`), with the quantity rules and the custom fields (`Requires.Custom`). File services are not listed. Archived and disabled services and categories the merchant's group may not see are never listed. Every price shown is remembered as the merchant's listed price (user rule 9).

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: This action takes no parameters.

QNT.description: `1` when the service sells more than one quantity.

QNTOPTIONS.description: The packs a service sells, comma separated; `""` when it sells a range.

type.description: `serviceimei`, `serviceserver` or `serviceremote`.

fieldname.description: The field name: what `CUSTOMFIELD` takes, matched without regard to letter case. The field key is still accepted.

fieldoptions.description: The choices of a dropdown, comma separated; `""` otherwise.

oneOf.title: placeimeiorder
oneOf.description: Place an IMEI, server or remote order. Orders a service at the merchant's own price and holds it from the wallet. `ID` is the `SERVICEID` of `imeiservicelist`; an IMEI service takes `IMEI`, a server or remote service its custom fields in `CUSTOMFIELD`. The answer is immediate: `REFERENCEID` is our order id (status 0). A price that rose more than the tolerance above the price last listed is refused with "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again."; a balance that is too low with "Not enough credits". A File service is placed with `placefileorder`.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

QNT.description: The quantity; defaults to the service's minimum.

CUSTOMFIELD.description: The values of the service custom fields by field name: base64 of a JSON object (an object is accepted too).

IMEI.description: The IMEI of an IMEI service (15 digits, Luhn); leave it out for a server or remote service.

oneOf.title: placeimeiorderbulk
oneOf.description: Place several orders. `parameters` is an object keyed by the caller's request id, each entry the parameters of `placeimeiorder`. The answer has one entry per request id: `{ "SUCCESS": [...] }` or `{ "ERROR": [...] }`. Each order is placed on its own (a refused one never stops the others); at most 100 per call. A request id has 1 to 64 characters. The call costs one point of the key’s per-minute limit per item (at most the whole limit).

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object keyed by your request id, one entry per order; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

QNT.description: The quantity; defaults to the service's minimum.

CUSTOMFIELD.description: The values of the service custom fields by field name: base64 of a JSON object (an object is accepted too).

IMEI.description: The IMEI of an IMEI service (15 digits, Luhn); leave it out for a server or remote service.

oneOf.title: getimeiorder
oneOf.description: Order status and result. `STATUS` 0 new, 1 in process, 3 rejected (refunded), 4 completed; `CODE` is the result of a completed order or the reason of a rejected one. Another account's order, and the account's own store order, like an unknown id, are an error.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

ID.description: The order: the `REFERENCEID` the placement answered.

CODE.description: The result of a completed order, the reason of a rejected one; `""` while it runs.

oneOf.title: getimeiorderbulk
oneOf.description: Status of several orders. `parameters` is an object keyed by the caller's request id, each entry `{ "ID": <order> }`; the answer has one entry per request id with the `STATUS` and `CODE` of `getimeiorder` or an error; at most 100 per call. A request id has 1 to 64 characters.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object keyed by your request id, one entry per order; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

ID.description: The order: the `REFERENCEID` the placement answered.

CODE.description: The result of a completed order, the reason of a rejected one; `""` while it runs.

oneOf.title: placefileorder
oneOf.description: Place a file order. Orders a File service. The file is `FILENAME` and `FILEDATA` (base64) in `parameters`, or a file part of a `multipart/form-data` request; it is stored like `POST /client/files` (up to 25 MiB). A form body of this endpoint may be up to 25 MiB (every other route keeps 1 MiB); `FILEDATA` is base64 inside the base64 `parameters`, so about 13 MiB of file fits a form: send a larger file as a multipart file part. Everything else is as `placeimeiorder`. A service that is not a File service is refused. If the order is refused (changed price, not enough credits), the uploaded file is not kept.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

QNT.description: The quantity; defaults to the service's minimum.

CUSTOMFIELD.description: The values of the service custom fields by field name: base64 of a JSON object (an object is accepted too).

FILENAME.description: The name of the file, when it is sent as `FILEDATA`.

FILEDATA.description: The file: base64 of its content. A multipart request may send the file as a file part instead.

oneOf.title: getfileorder
oneOf.description: Result of a file order. As `getimeiorder`; when the result is a file, `FILEID` is its id: the merchant opens the file from its portal (`GET /client/files/:id`).

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

ID.description: The order: the `REFERENCEID` the placement answered.

CODE.description: The result of a completed order, the reason of a rejected one; `""` while it runs.

placeimeiorder.summary: Place an IMEI, server or remote order

200.description: Always HTTP 200 with the headers `X-Powered-By: DHRU-FUSION` and `dhru-fusion-api-version: 6.1`. A success is `{ "SUCCESS": [ ... ], "apiversion": "6.1" }`; a refusal (a wrong credential, an unknown action, a rejected order) is `{ "ERROR": [ { "MESSAGE": "..." } ], "apiversion": "6.1" }`. A bulk action answers one `SUCCESS` or `ERROR` list per request id.

post.description: A key is a Dhru credential: it carries no scope, and a `scopes` field in the body is ignored. `allowedIps` takes up to 20 addresses or CIDR ranges (a bare address is stored as /32 or /128; bits after the prefix are refused); an empty list means any address. `expiresAt` must be in the future. The answer carries the full key once as `secret` (`Cache-Control: no-store`): only a keyed hash is stored, so a lost key cannot be shown again. The per-minute limit is the server default; only staff change it. A merchant may hold 10 live keys: the next one is `422` on `name`. Every new key sends the merchant a security notice by email. While the account's password is one staff set (a temporary password, until the merchant chooses a password from a link mailed to its address), and after a staff member who is not an Owner changed the account's email address (until an Owner changes it or confirms it), the route is `403 FORBIDDEN`. The rank and the status are read again from the account row, locked, before the key is stored: an account that is no longer of a merchant rank is `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED` and no key is made.
