post.description: The last sign-in step of an account with two-factor sign-in on, of any rank: it turns the pending session into a full one (a new session token). Needs the `X-CSRF-Token` of the pending session. Twenty wrong codes of one account within 24 hours close the step: every code, the right one included, is then refused with `429 RATE_LIMITED`, whose `Retry-After` is the seconds until it opens. The step opens again after 24 hours (counted from the first wrong code), or sooner with a password link (reset or invitation) or a 2FA reset by staff (also a temporary password from staff); a correct code never resets the count.

post.description: An alias of `POST /client/auth/sign-in`: the same use case, the same budget and the same lock, answering only `next`. It opens a session: `pending_password` (10 minutes) when staff set a temporary password that is not replaced yet (`next: password`: the caller shows a new-password form and calls `POST /client/auth/password/change`), `pending_totp` (10 minutes) when the account has two-factor sign-in on, a full one otherwise. One `401` answers an unknown email, a wrong password and an account with no password yet. Five attempts per email and network (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) in 15 minutes; ten failed attempts for one email (a success in between does not cancel them) lock it for 15 minutes for every network its account has not signed in from (the lock is shared with `POST /store/v1/auth/login` and `POST /client/auth/sign-in`): both answer `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, the same for every email. While the lock runs, the attempts a network the account has signed in from is still allowed share one budget per network: five in 15 minutes, then `429 RATE_LIMITED` like any other attempt. A temporary password works for 72 hours after it was set; after that it is refused like a wrong password. Send `X-Turnstile-Token`: production requires it (`TURNSTILE_MERCHANT_AUTH`, on by default there).

parameters.name: x-turnstile-token
parameters.description: The Cloudflare Turnstile widget's token (its `cf-turnstile-response` value). Send it now: the server requires it once the anti-bot check on this route is switched on (`TURNSTILE_MERCHANT_AUTH`), and then a missing or failed check answers `403 TURNSTILE_FAILED`. A token is single use and valid for five minutes, so a retried write needs a new one.

post.description: The one email and password form of every account, merchant rank or retail rank. An email is one account with a login (a guest is never found here), so there is nothing to choose between. The answer says which area the account belongs to: `rank.kind` is `merchant` or `retail` (`kind` says `merchant` or `customer` for the same fact, and stays until the contract release). The session cookie is the one cookie of every account, and the readable CSRF cookie is `csrf_token_client` for a merchant rank and `csrf_token_store` for the retail rank, with the `X-CSRF-Token` header. `next` is `password` after a temporary password (a `pending_password` session: continue with `POST /client/auth/password/change`), `totp` for an account with two-factor sign-in on (a `pending_totp` session: continue with `POST /client/auth/2fa`), or `done`. One `401` answers an unknown email, a wrong password, an account with no password yet and an erased account; `403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` comes only after a correct password. Every attempt counts against the one budget of `POST /client/auth/login` and `POST /store/v1/auth/login` (5 per email and network in 15 minutes) and ten failures (a success in between does not cancel them) lock the email for 15 minutes for every network the account being signed into has not signed in from, whatever the email is: both answer `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. While the lock runs, the attempts a network the account has signed in from is still allowed share one budget per network: five in 15 minutes, then `429 RATE_LIMITED` like any other attempt. A temporary password works for 72 hours after it was set; after that it is refused like a wrong password. Needs the anti-bot token (`X-Turnstile-Token`, always) and an `Origin` the API allows.

post.description: Uploads one file (`multipart/form-data` with one part named `file`, any media type, 1 byte to 25 MiB). The name is reduced to its base name without control characters (at most 200 characters). The object goes to the files bucket and a file owned by the account is recorded with its size and SHA-256. A missing or empty file is `422` on `file`; more than 25 MiB is `413`. The id is what an order or a bank transfer receipt refers to. Only accounts of a merchant rank use this route: a retail rank is refused with `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED` before the body is read. An account of a merchant rank can upload 500 files (5 GiB) in 24 hours; over the bound is `422` on `file` with the code `quota` (decisions 053 and 064: the quota follows the rank kind). A multipart body is read only when the request carries a live session (`401` before the body is read otherwise).

post.description: Writes a top-up invoice (status open, due in 14 days) through one of the merchant payment methods: `fee = amount x percent + fixed`, `netAmount = amount - fee` (the wallet is credited with it when the invoice is paid). A manual method answers `{ invoice, instructions }`; an automatic one opens a checkout and answers `{ invoice, paymentUrl }` (`502 GATEWAY_ERROR` when the gateway fails: the invoice reserved for it is voided). 422 on `gatewayId` for a method the merchant may not use, and on `amount` outside the method limits, above the group limit per deposit, too small for the fee, or (for an automatic method) with more decimals than it can charge exactly (`not_chargeable`, two for a card page). A card method asks for 3-D Secure while the shop's `require3ds` policy is on. A merchant holds at most five unpaid top-up invoices that are less than 24 hours old or have a receipt in review: the next one is `409 CONFLICT`, before any payment page is opened (decision 049). The optional `Idempotency-Key` header makes a retry answer the same invoice (`idempotency-replayed: true`); the same key with another gateway or amount is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` (decision 064). Only an account of a merchant rank may ask: another rank is `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`.

post.description: Orders a service at the merchant's own price (the one price resolver). The price is held from the wallet in the same transaction; an order that would cost more than the tolerance above the price the merchant last listed is refused (`PRICE_CHANGED`, with both prices), a smaller raise is charged and recorded; a second open order for the same service and input is refused under the service's `block_open` rule (`DUPLICATE_ORDER`). An IMEI service takes `imei` (15 digits, Luhn) or `imeis` (a bulk of up to 100: one order each, all placed or none); a server or remote service takes `inputs`; a File service a `fileId` and/or `inputs`. The answer is immediate: the orders are `pending`, in the manual queue or waiting for the dispatch job. Send an `Idempotency-Key` (a new one per form submission) so that a double click or a retry never places or holds twice: the same key and body sends the first `201` again with the response header `idempotency-replayed: true` (nothing is placed); another body with the key is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, one still running `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` (`Retry-After`). A refused request stores nothing, so the key may be sent again. The answer is kept 7 days; a replay is the first answer as it was (the orders may have moved on). Without the header nothing changes. An account that is not active is refused with `403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` and a frozen merchant wallet with `409 WALLET_FROZEN`; nothing is written (a retail rank never reaches this route: `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`).

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Makes a retry safe: the first answer is stored with the key and sent again for the same request; another request with the key is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, one still running `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. The answer is kept 7 days from the first request; after that the stored answer is gone and the same key places a new order.

schema.description: Makes a retry safe: the first answer is stored with the key and sent again for the same request; another request with the key is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, one still running `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. The answer is kept 7 days from the first request; after that the stored answer is gone and the same key places a new order.

imeis.description: A bulk order: one order of the same service per IMEI, placed all together or not at all.

get.description: The services the signed-in merchant may order, at the price it pays (client price, else group price, else the base price after the pricing rule, the group discount, rounding and the floor). Live and `active` services in an active category whose allowed groups are empty or include the merchant's group; archived and disabled services are never listed. Default order: category order, then name, so the client can group by `category`. Filters: `type`, `categoryId`; `q` searches name, code and category; `ids` (comma-separated service ids, at most 100, each a positive whole number) keeps only those services, in the same rows: an id that is unknown, archived, off or hidden from the merchant's group is simply absent, and a bad value is `422` on `ids`. The page range applies as for every list (default 25 rows), so send `_end=100` with up to 100 ids to read them all in one call; `x-total-count` counts the services found among them. Every price shown is remembered as the merchant's listed price (price protection, user rule 9), a request with `ids` included, so a request that the browser marks as started by another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` or `same-site`, without an `Origin` that is one of the shop's origins) is `403 CSRF_FAILED` and remembers nothing; the portal's own server calls, which carry neither header, are answered.

get.description: A server-sent event stream (`text/event-stream`) of the signed-in person (a staff member or an account): `ready` first, `hb` every 15 seconds, `notification.created`, `notification.read`, `unread.changed`, `resync` and `bye`; the data of every event is one line of JSON (docs/contract/realtime-events.md). A reconnect sends the last event id back (`Last-Event-ID`, or `cursor`) and gets what it missed, at most 50 items, else `resync`. At most 3 streams per session and 30 per address (429 for the next one), ended after 15 minutes (`bye max_age`) and when the session ends (`bye session_ended`). Only a request started by the page’s own site is answered: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the origins of the route’s audience (the console’s for `/admin`, the shop’s for `/client` and `/store/v1`); anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED`. A refusal is an ordinary problem+json answer before the stream starts. `503 UNAVAILABLE` when live updates are switched off or the server is full: keep polling.

post.description: The merchant’s message. A ticket that waited on the merchant goes back to `open`; the reply target restarts from this message. post.description: An alias of `POST /client/auth/sign-in` that answers only `next`: the same use case, the same budget and the same lock. Opens a session: a full one, a `pending_password` one when the account must change a temporary password first (`next` `password`: continue with `POST /client/auth/password/change`), or a `pending_totp` one when two-step sign-in is on (`next` `totp`: continue with `POST /client/auth/2fa`). One `401` answers an unknown email, a wrong password and an account with no password yet. A correct password on a suspended or blocked account is `403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`. Five attempts per email and network in 15 minutes, and ten failed attempts (a success in between does not cancel them) lock the email (known or not, so the answer never shows who has an account) for 15 minutes for every network its account has not signed in from: both answer `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. While the lock runs, the attempts a network the account has signed in from is still allowed share one budget per network: five in 15 minutes, then `429 RATE_LIMITED` like any other attempt. A temporary password works for 72 hours after it was set; after that it is refused like a wrong password. Needs the anti-bot token (`X-Turnstile-Token`). Accepted only with an `Origin` header that is one of the shop’s origins, like the public `/client` sign-in routes (`403 CSRF_FAILED` otherwise). Retired in the contract release.

post.description: Answers `204` whatever the email is, so it cannot be used to find out who has an account. The link is for the retail rank: an email the store does not know yet becomes a retail account when the link is used (self-signup, the link proves the mailbox); a merchant rank, a suspended, blocked or anonymized account, and a blocklisted email get nothing, with the same answer. The link is valid one hour and works once; up to three such links work at once (a fourth replaces the oldest), and at most five are mailed an hour per account; a request beyond that answers `204` and sends nothing. Counted per network and email, whether or not the email exists. Needs the anti-bot token (`X-Turnstile-Token`). Every answer sets an HttpOnly cookie that lives as long as the link and marks the browser that asked for it (`POST /store/v1/auth/verify` reads it).

post.description: Spends the link (single use), marks the email verified on first use, turns a guest of that email into an account holder and opens a session: the cookies and the `X-CSRF-Token` header come with the answer, which is the account (`AccountMe`) plus `requestedHere`, `maskedEmail`, `next`, `claimedOrders` and `claimSkipped`. `next` is `totp` when the account has two-step sign-in on (the session is then a `pending_totp` one, finished by `POST /client/auth/2fa`) and `done` otherwise. `claimGuestOrders: true` asks to move the orders and records of the guest row of the same email onto the account (the mailbox is proven by this link, only the retail rank is offered it): `claimedOrders` says how many moved, and `claimSkipped: busy` says the claim gave up because another request holds one of the rows (the sign-in itself still succeeded; ask for a new link later). In the browser that asked for the link (the cookie of `POST /store/v1/auth/magic-link`) it signs in as before (`requestedHere` true). Anywhere else, while the browser holds a live session of another account, it is `409 CONFLICT` (sign out first): that session stays and the link is not spent; in a browser without such a session it signs in with `requestedHere` false, and the shop shows whose account was opened. A link that is unknown, used, expired or replaced, or belongs to an account that may not act, or whose email gained a login account since the mail was sent, is `410 TOKEN_INVALID`; so is a link of a merchant rank, and so is a verification link: that one is answered by `POST /client/auth/verify-email`, which never opens a session (decision 052). Accepted only with an `Origin` header that is one of the shop’s origins, like the public `/client` sign-in routes (`403 CSRF_FAILED` otherwise).

claimGuestOrders.description: Move the orders of the guest row of this email onto the account (offered after the mailbox was proven); default false.

discountPercent.description: Exact decimal number as a string.

hasPassword.description: True once the account has a password; false for an account that signs in by link.

currency.description: The ISO code of the currency prices are shown in; null when none is chosen.

username.description: The Dhru username of a merchant rank; empty for a retail account.

requestedHere.description: True when this browser asked for the link (it carries the cookie of `POST /store/v1/auth/magic-link`); false for a link asked for in another browser or sent by the shop: the shop then shows whose account was opened (`maskedEmail`).

maskedEmail.description: The address of the account the link opened, masked (`da•••@example.com`).

next.description: `totp` when two-step sign-in still wants a code (a `pending_totp` session: finish with `POST /client/auth/2fa`), `done` otherwise.

claimedOrders.description: How many guest orders (and their records) moved onto the account; 0 when the box was not ticked or nothing matched.

claimSkipped.description: `busy` when the claim gave up because another request holds a row it needs: the sign-in still succeeded, ask for a new link later.

post.description: Starts a purchase, as a guest or as a signed-in retail account: the session locks the retail price, the tax rate of the buyer's `country` and the exchange rate of `currency` for 30 minutes. A guest's email makes (or finds) the guest record of that email: it never attaches to the login account of the email, whatever its rank. A request that carries the cookie of a signed-in account (and its `X-CSRF-Token`, else `403 CSRF_FAILED` and nothing is written) opens the checkout as that account instead: `email` must be the email of the account in any case (else `422` on `email`: "Use the email of your account, or sign out to check out as a guest."), the `guestCheckout` switch does not apply and the session belongs to the signed-in account. A signed-in merchant rank is refused (`403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`, "Your account orders from its price list.") and nothing is written. A request without a usable account session is a guest. An IMEI service needs a valid `imei` (else `422 INVALID_IMEI`); a service with order fields needs their `inputs`. An account or guest record that may not act is refused (`403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`), and so is a guest whose email belongs to a login account that is suspended, blocked or erased, with the same answer as a blocklist hit and no guest record made; when the shop requires an account (`guestCheckout` off) a guest gets `401 UNAUTHORIZED`. A service the shop cannot sell is `422` on `serviceId`. While the shop has a tax window in force for any country, a `country` without one is `422` on `country` (code `unsupported`, "Choose a country."), the refusal of the customer profile; a shop with no tax window in force accepts any country without tax. While the `country` has a regional tax window in force, `region` must name a region that has one (any case), else `422` on `region` (code `unsupported`, "Choose a region."); the national window alone does not apply then. An email that staff blocked for guest checkouts is refused to a guest like any blocked email (`403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`) and accepted for its signed-in account (decision 050). The answer carries the session token: the whole credential of the next two routes. Paying comes later. Needs the anti-bot token (`X-Turnstile-Token`). The answer holds the token, so it is never cached. `currency` must be on offer in `GET /store/v1/config` (`422` on `currency` otherwise).

post.description: Pays an open checkout from the signed-in retail account's store balance (USD) and creates the order **at once**, in one transaction: no gateway, no webhook, no polling. Besides the checkout token in the path, the request needs the account session cookie and its `X-CSRF-Token`: `401 UNAUTHORIZED` means "sign in to pay from the balance" (not an ended checkout). The checkout must belong to that account **and** have been opened while signed in (`balancePayable` on the checkout), else `403 FORBIDDEN`. The account must hold the retail rank when the payment is made (checked under the account's row lock), else `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED` and nothing is paid. A paid, expired or no-longer-sold checkout is `409 INVALID_TRANSITION`, an account that may not act `403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, missing consents `422` on `consent`, a balance below the gross `402 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, a balance on hold `409 WALLET_FROZEN`, the store balance switched off `409 WALLET_DISABLED`. `Idempotency-Key` is required: a retry with the same key answers the same payment and order (header `idempotency-replayed: true`, the wallet as it is now); a key a `/pay` call already used on this checkout is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. The ledger posts Dr customer wallet / Cr customer funds / Cr VAT payable (VAT at spend, at the rate the checkout locked).

post.description: Writes proof of what the buyer agreed to: for each purpose (`terms`, `privacy`, `refund_policy`, `withdrawal_waiver`, `marketing`) one record with the version of the current legal document (`terms`, `privacy` and `refund_policy` have one; the waiver and marketing do not), the time and the buyer's IP. A repeat of the latest record changes nothing. The records belong to the account of the checkout: the signed-in account that opened it, or the guest record of its email. When that is an account with a login, `marketing` is not recorded and is left out of `records`: only the account's own page changes it. The exception is the account holder: a request that also carries the cookie and `X-CSRF-Token` of that account's signed-in session records `marketing` too, and the account's marketing choice (`marketingOptIn`) follows the answer; an account session without its CSRF header is `403 CSRF_FAILED` and a merchant-rank session `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`, and nothing is written. `422` when a purpose has no published document or a purpose is listed twice; `409 INVALID_TRANSITION` when the session is paid or expired. The answer says whether the session now has every required consent. The token in the path is the credential.

post.summary: Record the consents of a checkout

post.description: Starts the payment of an open checkout with one of the methods `GET /store/v1/checkout-sessions/:token` lists (`gateway` is its `code`): the gateway opens a hosted page for the session's locked gross in the buyer's currency (3-D Secure for a card when the shop asks for it, a wallet or a crypto address on the same page) and the answer carries its address. **No order exists yet**: the order is created, the money booked and the service delivered only when the gateway's signed confirmation arrives (`POST /webhooks/payments/:gateway`), in one transaction. The checkout needs every required consent first (`422` on `consent`); a paid or expired checkout is `409 INVALID_TRANSITION` (so is a page that opened after its payment was already closed, and so is a checkout whose service the shop no longer sells at all: switched off, unlisted or without a retail price; a changed price is not a reason, the locked price holds), an account or guest record that may not act `403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, a method that is off or does not take the amount `422` on `gateway`, a gateway that cannot open its page `502 GATEWAY_ERROR`. `Idempotency-Key` is required. The token in the path is the credential; a request that carries an account session needs its `X-CSRF-Token` (`403 CSRF_FAILED`), and a merchant-rank session is `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`, as on the consents step (nothing is written). A checkout keeps at most 3 payment pages open (`429 RATE_LIMITED` for another; a page that failed, was paid or is held frees its place); an amount the method cannot charge exactly is `422` on `gateway` (`not_chargeable`); a `returnUrl` that is not an address of this shop is `422` on `returnUrl` (`not_shop`). The confirmation creates the order only once the gateway's own record says the payment succeeded for this amount and currency; a payment made more than 30 minutes after the price lock ended is not used at the old price (decision 048).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The checkout token.

post.description: Uploads one file from the signed-in account (`multipart/form-data` with one part named `file`): a PDF, JPEG or PNG of 1 byte to 5 MiB, such as the receipt of a store balance top-up (`POST /store/v1/me/wallet/top-ups/:id/receipt` takes its id). The file belongs to the account. Another media type is `422` on `file` (`type`); an empty file `422` (`empty`); a body over 5 MiB is refused before it is parsed, whether or not it declares its length (`413`). Counted against the `upload` limiter (20 a minute per address). An account of a retail rank can upload 30 files (100 MiB) in 24 hours, ticket files included (`422` on `file`, `quota`: the quota follows the rank kind, decision 064). A merchant rank is refused with `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED` before the body is read. A multipart body is read only when the request carries a live session (`401` before the body is read otherwise).

post.description: The link at the bottom of a marketing email. Switches marketing off for the account the token names: `marketing_opt_in` becomes false and a consent record (`granted: false`, the caller’s address and user agent) is added, so the next campaign and the sending of a message already queued leave the account out. Repeating it changes nothing. Public by design: it has no session and no anti-bot token, because mailbox providers call it themselves (RFC 8058 one-click: a form body `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`) and the site’s page calls it with no body. The token is a keyed MAC over the account id: it can switch marketing off, never on. A link sent before the accounts were merged names an old customer number, which is looked up in the legacy id map (never read as an account id). An account that is unknown or erased, and an old number the map does not know, answer `204` too (nothing to say, nothing to leak); a token that does not verify is `410`.

get.description: A server-sent event stream (`text/event-stream`) of the signed-in person (a staff member or an account): `ready` first, `hb` every 15 seconds, `notification.created`, `notification.read`, `unread.changed`, `resync` and `bye`; the data of every event is one line of JSON (docs/contract/realtime-events.md). A reconnect sends the last event id back (`Last-Event-ID`, or `cursor`) and gets what it missed, at most 50 items, else `resync`. At most 3 streams per session and 30 per address (429 for the next one), ended after 15 minutes (`bye max_age`) and when the session ends (`bye session_ended`). Only a request started by the page’s own site is answered: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or an `Origin` that is one of the origins of the route’s audience (the console’s for `/admin`, the shop’s for `/client` and `/store/v1`); anything else is `403 CSRF_FAILED`. A refusal is an ordinary problem+json answer before the stream starts. `503 UNAVAILABLE` when live updates are switched off or the server is full: keep polling.

get.description: The signed-in customer’s own tickets: every ticket whose requester is the customer, those filed on the public form with the same address included once their link has been opened (decision 053). Newest activity first (`updatedAt` descending); sort by `updatedAt` or `createdAt`; filter by `status` (repeat the key for IN; `pending` means the team waits for the customer); at most 50 a page; there is no search. Each row carries the ticket `token`: open the conversation with the token routes (`GET /store/v1/tickets/:token`, `…/stream`, `…/messages`). A row is `hasUnread` while support wrote a message the page has not marked as seen (`POST …/read`). A ticket that has no link any more (its token was cleared by an erasure) is not listed. Never cached (`Cache-Control: no-store`): the rows hold credentials. The link of a ticket resolved more than 180 days ago no longer opens it (`404` on the token routes).

post.description: Starts a store balance top-up: `amount` (USD, what the customer pays; the fee comes out of it) through `gatewayId`. A manual method answers the transfer `instructions` (then upload the receipt); an automatic one answers the `paymentUrl`. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required: a retry with the same key and body answers the same top-up (`idempotency-replayed: true`); the same key with another body is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Limits answer `422` on `amount` (`min`, `max`, `fee`, `daily_count`, `daily_amount`, `max_balance`, and `not_chargeable` for an automatic method that cannot charge the amount exactly: a card page takes two decimals) or `409 CONFLICT` (three unpaid top-ups). Refused while the balance is switched off (`WALLET_DISABLED`), and through an automatic method while it is on hold (`WALLET_FROZEN`). A card method asks for 3-D Secure while the shop's `require3ds` policy is on (decision 049). The creates of one account run one at a time, and a change of rank either lands first (the create is then `403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED`) or waits for it (decision 064).

get.description: The service pages that are switched on, at the retail price: `net` before tax, `tax` of the buyer's country and `gross`, in the buyer's currency (`buyerCountry`, `currency`). Only services the shop may sell and has priced appear (an archived, disabled or B2B-only service never does, and the price is never under the retail floor). Filter by `brand`, `network` and `country` (case-insensitive), `featured`, `type` (`imei`, `server`, `remote`, `file`; repeat the key for several), `categoryId` (repeatable) and `availability` (`in_stock` keeps the services the stock covers); `minPrice` and `maxPrice` bound `price.gross` in the requested `currency` (inclusive; `minPrice` above `maxPrice` is `422` on `maxPrice`); `q` searches title, summary, brand and network; sort by `featured` (default: featured first), `sort`, `title`, `popular` (best sellers: the orders of the last 30 days, refreshed every 30 minutes, no number is shown), `listedAt` (first publication), `price` (`gross`, in the requested currency) and `relevance` (how well the service matches `q`; the default order while `q` is set, ignored otherwise). With `q` the order and the match set come from the search engine, which forgives typos and knows synonyms; `x-search-engine: typesense|fallback` says which answered, and with a price sort or price bounds the set is the best 1000 matches (`x-search-truncated: true` when more matched). post.description: Opens a ticket from the order page or the contact page, with no account. `orderToken` (the tracking token of the order) links the ticket to the order and to its customer; without it `email` is needed, and a first-time address becomes a guest customer. An unknown or non-storefront `orderToken` is `422` on `orderToken`. The ticket starts `new` with the priority of its category and a reply target; the customer gets a receipt email whose link holds the ticket token, the whole credential of the next three routes. The answer carries `token` only when `orderToken` was given (the caller already holds the order link); with `email` alone it has no token, because anyone can type an address and the ticket is filed under the customer who owns it: the receipt link is the only way in. An address may get 3 new tickets an hour (case-insensitive), counted for the typed `email` and, with `orderToken`, for the address of the order's customer: the fourth is `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. The receipt email repeats nothing that was typed (no name, no subject): it holds the ticket number and the link. A ticket opened with a typed `email` is listed in that customer’s account only once its link has been opened (decision 053). Needs the anti-bot token (`X-Turnstile-Token`). Never cached: the answer holds a credential or sits behind it.

post.description: One file (`multipart/form-data`, one part named `file`): a PDF, JPEG or PNG of 1 byte to 5 MiB whose content starts with the type's magic bytes. Another type, or a content that is not what it claims, is `422` on `file` (`type`); an empty file `422` (`empty`); more than 5 MiB `413`: a body over 5 MiB is refused before it is parsed, whether or not it declares its length. The answer is the stored file; its id goes into `fileIds` of the next message. There is no virus scan: files are never shown inline, only downloaded through a link. The file belongs to the ticket's customer. A resolved ticket is closed for the customer: `409 TICKET_RESOLVED` and nothing is stored (staff reopen the ticket first). Counted against `upload` (20 a minute per address). A ticket link can upload 20 files (50 MiB) in 24 hours, and its customer 30 (100 MiB) (`422` on `file`, `quota`; decision 053).

get.description: A server-sent event stream (`text/event-stream`) of the ticket the token opens: `ready` first, `hb` every 15 seconds, then `ticket.message.created` (a new public message, with `id: t<message id>`), `ticket.updated` and `ticket.read`, in the requester view (docs/contract/realtime-events.md); never an internal note or a staff name. The ticket is matched by `number` (`ticketId` is null). A reconnect sends the last event id back (`Last-Event-ID`, or `cursor`) and gets the messages it missed, at most 100, else `resync`. No cookie is involved: the token in the path is the credential, as for the other ticket routes. At most 3 streams per ticket and 30 per address (`429`), 20 opens a minute per ticket; ended after 15 minutes (`bye max_age`) and at once when the link stops working (`bye session_ended`, an anonymized customer: the token then answers `404`). `503 UNAVAILABLE` when live updates are switched off: the page keeps refreshing every 30 seconds. Lookups count against the token limit (30 a minute per address).

get.summary: Live events of a support ticket

post.description: A payment gateway reports a dispute. The delivery must carry the gateway's signature (the scheme of its driver; either of the gateway's two webhook secrets), a signed time within 5 minutes of now and an event id not seen before; otherwise `400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. `dispute.created` records the dispute once (the gateway id is unique per payment) with its evidence deadline and marks the payment `disputed` and the order timeline; an update of a dispute that is open at the gateway (`charge.dispute.updated` or `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn` with status `needs_response` or `under_review`) records it the same way when it is not recorded yet. A card network inquiry (a status that starts with `warning_`) records nothing and is acknowledged with `200`. A dispute won returns the payment to `captured` (or `partial_refund`/`refunded` when refunds completed), unless another dispute of the payment is lost (`chargeback`) or still open (`disputed`); a dispute lost posts the chargeback journal once and marks the payment `chargeback`, and closes the refunds of the payment the gateway has not paid (their journals reversed, decision 048). A repeat of an event answers `200` and changes nothing; event types the shop does not use are acknowledged with `200`; an event that names a payment not recorded yet, a payment held for staff, or a closed dispute whose opening was not recorded yet answers `503 UNAVAILABLE`, so the gateway delivers it again (decision 048; once the event is 24 hours old it is acknowledged with `200` and reported for staff). A delivery the database could not apply because it met another change at the same moment writes nothing and answers `503 UNAVAILABLE` as well, so the gateway delivers it again.

post.description: A payment gateway confirms a top-up. The delivery must carry the gateway's signature (the scheme of its driver), a signed time within 5 minutes of now and an event id not seen before; otherwise `400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. A confirmed payment of an open invoice is recorded once (the gateway reference is unique): the payment waits `payments.auto_credit_delay_minutes` (at least the gateway hold hours), then a job asks the gateway again and credits the wallet. A repeat of the same event answers `200` and changes nothing. Events billing does not use are acknowledged with `200`. A gateway may keep two webhook secrets: a delivery signed with either passes. Refund results (`refund.updated` with a final status, `refund.failed`) settle the storefront refund they name, and dispute events are handled exactly as on `POST /webhooks/disputes/:gateway` (one provider endpoint with every event is enough; the same dispute on both URLs is recorded once). For a storefront payment (`PAY-<id>`) the gateway's own record is read before the order is created: when it cannot be read the answer is `502 GATEWAY_ERROR` and the gateway delivers the event again (once the event is 24 hours old the payment is held for staff instead); a payment the record does not show as paid, or shows for another amount or currency, and a confirmation that does not state its amount or currency, is held for staff: nothing is created, and money that arrived is sent back in full automatically when the gateway can refund. A payment made more than 30 minutes after the checkout's price lock ended is refunded at once, or waits in the risk queue when the method cannot refund. A confirmation of a top-up invoice that is paid or void is recorded for staff review and never credited. A dispute event for a payment or a dispute not recorded yet is `503 UNAVAILABLE`, so the gateway delivers it again (decision 048).

capabilityToken.description: An unguessable token in the path (checkout, order tracking, support ticket or sign-in link) that authorises exactly one record. Sent by email or shown once; stored only as a hash.

customerSession.name: gsm_client_session
customerSession.description: Session cookie of an account of the retail rank (a shop account), set by the sign-in routes under `/client/auth` (password) or `/store/v1/auth` (sign-in link). It is the same cookie as `merchantSession`, because there is one session cookie for every account; the older `gsm_store_session` is never read. HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send `X-CSRF-Token`, whose readable cookie is `csrf_token_store` for the retail rank and `csrf_token_client` for a merchant rank.

dhruCredentials.description: Dhru Fusion credentials are not an HTTP header: send `username` and `apiaccesskey` as form fields in the request body. The key has an optional list of allowed IP addresses and its own requests-per-minute limit.

gatewaySignature.description: Payment gateway webhook, verified per gateway with its signing secret. Deliveries outside a 5-minute window are refused and events are de-duplicated by the gateway event id.

merchantSession.name: gsm_client_session
merchantSession.description: Session cookie of an account of a merchant rank, set by the sign-in routes under `/client/auth`. It is the one session cookie of every account: the same cookie opens a retail account (see `customerSession`), and the rank of the account decides which routes it may call (`403 RANK_NOT_ALLOWED` on the others). HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send `X-CSRF-Token`.

metricsAccess.description: Prometheus scrape access: loopback and private networks, or `Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>`. When a token is configured it is required from every caller.

staffSession.name: gsm_admin_session
staffSession.description: Staff session cookie, set by the sign-in steps under `/admin/auth` (password, then the 2FA code). HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send the `X-CSRF-Token` header returned by sign-in. The permission a route needs is shown in `x-gsm-permission`.

urlSecret.description: A secret path segment (for example `/webhooks/{provider}/{secret}`) that only the provider knows; a wrong secret answers as if the route did not exist.

x-gsm-supplier-calls.description: Asks the supplier how much prepaid credit we have. The standard spells the answer key `AccoutInfo` (sic); `AccountInfo` is accepted too (when both come, a well-formed `AccoutInfo` wins and a malformed one gives way to `AccountInfo`). A missing block or a credit that is not a number is an unusable answer: the call is logged as failed. Extra fields are ignored. An answer larger than 256 KiB is not read. A balance outside -1000000000 to 1000000000 is read but not saved (decision 051).

transport.note: The form fields are `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action`, `requestformat=JSON` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object). The call is made by the worker or by a staff action, with the supplier's own account.

AccoutInfo.description: The balance block, spelled as in the Dhru standard.

credit.description: Our prepaid balance at the supplier, in its own currency. Read as a number: `"$1,200.50"` is accepted. Outside -1000000000 to 1000000000 it is not saved.

currency.description: The currency of the balance, for example `USD`. Optional.

mail.description: The e-mail of our account at the supplier. Optional.

AccountInfo.description: The balance block with the corrected spelling.

credit.description: Our prepaid balance at the supplier, in its own currency. Read as a number: `"$1,200.50"` is accepted. Outside -1000000000 to 1000000000 it is not saved.

currency.description: The currency of the balance, for example `USD`. Optional.

mail.description: The e-mail of our account at the supplier. Optional.

MESSAGE.description: Why the supplier refused, for example `Authentication Failed` or `Not enough credits`.

x-gsm-supplier-calls.summary: The supplier's services and their cost
x-gsm-supplier-calls.description: Asks for the whole catalogue: `LIST` is an object of groups, each with a `SERVICES` object of services. The client keeps each service once (the first one wins when an id repeats) and leaves out a service without an id, a name or a readable price; a field of the wrong type counts as missing, and every `Requires.*` flag is kept. The log keeps the count of services, not the list. The answer is read up to 16 MiB. Texts are kept without control characters: ids to 200 characters; names, groups, types and times to 300. A service whose price is not a number from 0 to 1000000000 is left out like one without a price, and counted (decision 051).

transport.note: The form fields are `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action`, `requestformat=JSON` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object). The call is made by the worker or by a staff action, with the supplier's own account.

LIST.description: The groups by name. A list that is missing or empty means the supplier has no services.

GROUPNAME.description: The group name; the key of the group in `LIST` when it is missing.

SERVICES.description: The services of the group by id. A group without `SERVICES` is skipped.

SERVICEID.description: The supplier's service id; the key of the entry in `SERVICES` when it is missing.

SERVICETYPE.description: `IMEI`, `SERVER` or `REMOTE`; used when the group has no `GROUPTYPE`.

SERVICENAME.description: The name (kept to 300 characters). A service without a name is left out.

CREDIT.description: The price in supplier credits. A service without a readable price, or with a price outside 0 to 1000000000, is left out.

TIME.description: The delivery time as text, for example `1-2 hours`.

QNT.description: `1` when the service takes a quantity, `0` when it does not. Kept in the synced entry; the import reads it (B213).

MINQNT.description: The smallest quantity of one order. Kept in the synced entry; the import reads it.

MAXQNT.description: The largest quantity of one order. Kept in the synced entry; the import reads it.

QNTOPTIONS.description: Pack sizes, comma separated (for example `5,10,25`); empty when the service sells a range. Kept in the synced entry; the import reads it and copies the rule into a service only when it creates that service.

Requires.Custom.description: The custom fields the service needs: `{ type, fieldname, fieldtype, description, fieldoptions, required }` each.

CUSTOM.description: The main box of the service: `{ allow, customname, customlen, maxlength, regex, ... }`. With `allow` 1 and a `customname` that is not an IMEI, the buyer types that value instead of an IMEI and it is sent as `IMEI`; the import makes such an IMEI service a server service whose first field is that box (decision 042). Kept in the synced entry; not read by the sync.

MESSAGE.description: Why the supplier refused, for example `Authentication Failed` or `Not enough credits`.

x-gsm-supplier-calls.summary: Send an order to the supplier
x-gsm-supplier-calls.description: Places one order and keeps the `REFERENCEID` of the answer (kept to 200 characters, without control characters) as the supplier reference. An answer without a REFERENCEID is unusable: the order goes to attention, it is never sent again by itself. The bulk variant `placeimeiorderbulk` (parameters keyed by a request id) is described by the Dhru standard but this backend never sends it: each order is its own job, so a refusal never stops another order and every order has its own log row. The parameters are sent in the form the supplier reads (`param_format`, decision 042): the classic XML string `<PARAMETERS><ID>..</ID><IMEI>..</IMEI><QNT>..</QNT></PARAMETERS>` (`dhru_xml`, the default of a Dhru supplier) or base64 of a JSON object (`json`). An answer larger than 256 KiB is not read; the order then goes to attention like any unusable answer (decision 051).

transport.note: The form fields are `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action`, `requestformat=JSON` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object). The call is made by the worker or by a staff action, with the supplier's own account.

IMEI.description: The main input: the IMEI, else the value of the field flagged as the main input (decisions 042 and 065), else the first required field. Left out when the order has none.

CUSTOMFIELD.description: The custom field values by the supplier's field names; never the field sent as `IMEI`. On the wire it is base64 of this JSON object in both parameter forms (decisions 026 and 042).

REFERENCEID.description: The supplier's reference of the order.

MESSAGE.description: Why the supplier refused, for example `Authentication Failed` or `Not enough credits`.

x-gsm-supplier-calls.summary: Ask the supplier for the status of an order
x-gsm-supplier-calls.description: `STATUS` 4 is completed and 3 rejected; `CODE` is the result of a completed order or the reason of a rejected one. 0 and 1 mean the order is still running (2 is accepted as running too; the standard does not use it) and the CODE is ignored. A missing or unknown STATUS is an unusable answer: the order stays as it is and is asked again. The bulk variant `getimeiorderbulk` is described by the Dhru standard but this backend never sends it: each poll job asks about one order. `CODE` is kept without control characters, to 20000 characters; an answer larger than 256 KiB is not read (decision 051).

transport.note: The form fields are `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action`, `requestformat=JSON` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object). The call is made by the worker or by a staff action, with the supplier's own account.

ID.description: The supplier's reference of the order: the `REFERENCEID` of the placement.

STATUS.description: 0 new, 1 in process, 3 rejected (refunded), 4 completed. Text such as `"4"` is accepted.

CODE.description: The result of a completed order, the reason of a rejected one; empty while it runs.

MESSAGE.description: Why the supplier refused, for example `Authentication Failed` or `Not enough credits`.
